business.what: Two reported segments: the Mobility Division (electric buses of 7, 9 and 12 metres and coaches, plus electric tippers; 86% of FY26 revenue) and the Energy Division (composite polymer insulators for transmission lines, substations, railways and distribution; 14%). Olectra was India's first e-bus maker (2017) and is the largest maker of composite insulators in India (company).
business.plants: Insulators and the original bus line in Hyderabad. New greenfield EV plant on 150 acres at Seetharampur (Chevella, Telangana): partial operations from 2025 with 2,500 units per shift; capacity 5,000 EVs a year, scalable to 10,000 (Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 presentations). SBI sanctioned a Rs500 cr term loan for it (Rs199.6 cr drawn at Mar-26, 9.05%, 20 quarterly instalments from Q1FY27); date of commercial operation declared 31-Dec-2025 (AR FY26 note 17).
business.technology: Technology collaboration with BYD (China) for batteries, chassis, components and spares (ICRA, Oct-2025); BYD Blade batteries in 40-50% of Q4FY26 deliveries (Sovrenn summary of the 1-Jun-2026 call). A new bus platform is due in Q3FY27 and an in-house e-truck platform (28-55 tonne) in Q4FY27 (AR FY26 chairman's message; Q1FY27 call).
business.units: Electric vehicles sold: 259 (FY22), 580 (FY23), 541 (FY24), 972 (FY25), 1,280 (FY26, +32%), 358 in Q1FY27 (161 in Q1FY26). 3,800+ vehicles on the road (AR FY26).
business.market: Domestic e-bus sales 5,423 units in FY26, ~30% growth (AR FY26 chairman's message); KPMG (Mar-2026, in AR FY26): 4.9k e-buses in FY26, of which 4.6k public; ~46,000 e-buses awarded for deployment over 2-3 years. Olectra: '20%+' share (MD&A); ~24% on its own unit count; 'over 30%' per the Q1FY27 call.
business.orderBook: ~10,000 buses at Mar-26 (AR FY26 MD&A: 55% 9-metre, 45% 12-metre and coaches); 10,193 at Jun-2025 (ICRA). 'Over 8,000' at the Q1FY27 call (17-Aug-2026), to be executed over two years, including ~4,000 for MSRTC and ~2,000 for BEST Mumbai (Sovrenn; the BEST buses go through Evey Trans (MUM)). FY26 wins: 1,085 buses for TGSRTC under CESL/PM E-DRIVE (via Evey Trans (NSK)) and 700 for BMTC Bengaluru (Evey matched the L1 price; CESL confirmation of quantity), per the AR FY26 AGM notice.

msrtc.order: LoI from MSRTC in Jul-2023 for 5,150 electric buses on wet lease, supply plus 12 years of maintenance, ~Rs10,000 cr (press), executed through Evey Trans (MSR) and (MAH).
msrtc.delays: On 26-May-2025 the Maharashtra transport minister ordered the contract cancelled after no bus was delivered by the extended 22-May-2025 deadline for 1,000 buses (FPJ). A revised schedule followed (620 buses by end-2025, 2,100 in 2026, the rest in 2027, press). By 1-Apr-2026 about 1,200 of 5,150 had been delivered; the deadline was extended to Dec-2026; reasons: supply constraints at the manufacturer and depots not ready (The Hitavada).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Olectra Greentech, consolidated, Rs crore, Screener basis (Screener's other income includes the share of profit of the Evey Trans SPV associates). Revenue growth and EBITDA margin come from the two-segment build below (vehicles x revenue per vehicle for the Mobility Division; growth for the Energy Division; segment EBIT as the company reports it), synced by OLECTRA.ctx.js: EBITDA = segment EBIT - bridge + model depreciation, where the bridge is the other income that the company books inside segment results. Net profit is attributable (OLECTRA.patch.js); minorities (~Rs2 cr) are carried in the tax rate.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the segment build. FY27E: 1,850 vehicles (Q1FY27 358; management guides 2,000-2,500 with ~500 in Q2 and 600-700 in Q4, but delivered only 64% of its ~2,000 FY26 target) at Rs1.40 cr of Mobility revenue per vehicle (Q1FY27 Rs1.38 cr, FY26 Rs1.55 cr; more 9-metre TGSRTC buses), insulators +20%. FY28-29E: 2,400 / 2,800 vehicles as the 5,000-a-year Seetharampur plant fills on an ~8,000-bus order book (MSRTC ~4,000, BEST ~2,000, TGSRTC 1,085, BMTC 700) and the e-truck starts.
assumptions._marginWhy: From the segment build: Mobility EBIT 9.0% / 9.5% / 9.5% (FY25 11.9%, FY26 9.8%, Q1FY27 8.2%) and insulators 24% (FY25 25.6%, FY26 34.5%, Q1FY27 22.1%). Screener-basis EBITDA margin FY26 14.3%, Q1FY27 11.8%; management's band is 12-15%, normalising to 10-12% in the long run.
assumptions._capexWhy: Q1FY27 call: ~Rs450 cr for new bus and truck platforms and ~Rs150 cr of infrastructure; Q4FY26 call: ~Rs400 cr over FY27-28; e-truck ~Rs400 cr over two years (overlapping). FY25 Rs177 cr, FY26 Rs159 cr. We take Rs250 / 250 / 150 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: Set in OLECTRA.ctx.js check: the Seetharampur plant was capitalised from 31-Dec-2025; Q1FY27 depreciation Rs14.6 cr (Rs58 cr a year) against Rs44.8 cr in FY26.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt; cash is mostly margin money and the investments are equity in Evey Trans SPVs, so no treasury yield. Interest on deposits and the associates' share of profit are in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built, not plugged. FY26 Rs22.4 cr (Screener) = interest Rs11.2 cr (mostly on margin-money deposits) + FX gain Rs2.1 cr + miscellaneous Rs1.0 cr (AR FY26 note 23) + share of associates' profit Rs8.1 cr. Q1FY27 Rs4.7 cr (other income Rs2.1 cr + associates Rs2.5 cr); four quarters to Jun-26 Rs20 cr. FY27E Rs20 cr: deposit interest ~Rs10 cr, associates ~Rs10 cr, no FX gain assumed; associates' share rises with the SPV fleets in FY28-29E.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance costs (working-capital loans, plant term loan, bank charges)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs61 cr after Rs13.7 cr was capitalised into the new plant; Q1FY27 Rs23.6 cr (+97%) once capitalisation stopped and working-capital loans rose. FY27E Rs95 cr (Q1 x4); Rs110-115 cr in FY28-29E as working capital and the platform/truck capex lift net debt in our model.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective tax plus the minority share: FY26 27.9% (tax 27.1% + minorities 0.8%), FY25 26.1%, Q1FY27 25.3%. 26.5%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs0.60 a share on EPS Rs21.62 (2.8%); FY25 Rs0.40.

build._note: Two-segment build (Rs crore). FY26 base = AR FY26 note 34. Mobility revenue = vehicles x revenue per vehicle (includes services, spares and bus-operation revenue). Segment EBIT is profit before interest and tax as reported; it includes other income and the associates' share, so bridge = otherIncome (FY24 Rs19 cr, FY25 Rs14 cr, FY26 Rs22 cr, Q1FY27 Rs5 cr: see OLECTRA.ctx.js).
build._why: Vehicles: FY26 1,280 (+32%); Q1FY27 358 (+122%). Guidance 2,000-2,500 for FY27; Olectra delivered 64% of its FY26 target (~2,000 guided, 1,280 delivered; MSRTC deliveries ~1,200 of 5,150 by Apr-2026), so 1,850 / 2,400 / 2,800 (FY29E = 56% of the 5,000 plant). Revenue per vehicle Rs1.40 / 1.43 / 1.46 cr (FY26 Rs1.55 cr, Q1FY27 Rs1.38 cr; more 9-metre buses in the TGSRTC/BMTC orders, trucks from Q4FY27). Mobility EBIT 9.0% / 9.5% / 9.5%: Q1FY27 8.2%, FY26 9.8%, FY25 11.9%; tender pricing and a new plant's fixed costs offset softer raw materials. Insulators: FY26 +81% (Rs325 cr) with a 34.5% EBIT margin, Q1FY27 +47% but 22.1%; management targets 5x revenue in three years (new products, capacity, exports): +20% / +18% / +15% at 24%.

dcf._betaWhy: Tender-driven volumes, one group customer (Evey) for most sales, technology dependence on BYD and a small-cap retail-held stock. Net debt is small (~2-5% of enterprise value), so WACC is close to the cost of equity; beta 1.15 gives 13.4%.
dcf._tgWhy: House range 5-6%: 6%, as bus electrification has decades to run (penetration ~5-7% in FY26).
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~18% to 9% over ten years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin 11% in steady state: management's own long-run band is 10-12%.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 3% of revenue (FY24-26: 7-15% while the plant was built); depreciation 2.2%. Working capital stays at ~30% of revenue (the engine holds the FY26 ratio).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Deliveries hit guidance (2,300+ in FY27E, 3,500 by FY29E) as MSRTC, BEST and TGSRTC buses flow from the new plant, e-trucks find MEIL and outside buyers, and insulators keep FY26-like margins: growth ~8pp a year higher and EBITDA margin +1pp.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Execution slips again (depots, BYD parts, Evey's funding), MSRTC or another STU cancels part of an order, Evey pays more slowly so Olectra borrows more, and tender prices squeeze margins: growth ~10pp a year lower and EBITDA margin -1.5pp.

methods.why: How the street and the market value Olectra: P/E on forward EPS (Geojit, the only broker with published calls, valued it on P/E; no broker note dated Sep-2025 to Sep-2026 found). Multiple derived in tools/authoring/OLECTRA.ctx.js: own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 (no trough years) times the auto-OEM sector de-rating at 30-Sep-2026 (PLAYBOOK 4, 7c), nearest half-turn; written by syncMultiples().

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Separates the operating business from net debt. Multiple derived in OLECTRA.ctx.js from the stock's own trailing EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021 and the same sector move, restated from trailing to Sep-28E EBITDA; net debt (SPV equity at book counted as investments) deducted.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 10-year FCFF at 13.4% (cost of equity, close to WACC with little debt) and 6% terminal growth, less net debt. Working capital stays at ~30% of revenue.

cover.headline: India's first e-bus maker sells three-quarters of its output to its parent's operator: the house multiple says BUY, the cash flows say be careful
cover.lead: Olectra Greentech makes electric buses (86% of FY26 revenue) and composite insulators (14%). Its parent, the MEIL group, also owns Evey Trans, which wins state gross-cost contracts and buys the buses: 75% of FY26 revenue and 72% of receivables were with related parties. Revenue grew 8x in five years to ₹2,312 cr and EPS reached ₹21.62, but FY26 profit growth came from insulators, and Q1FY27 revenue +66% brought no profit growth as interest doubled. We forecast 1,850 / 2,400 / 2,800 vehicles (guidance 2,000-2,500 for FY27) and EPS of ₹20.8 / ₹29.3 / ₹36.0 for FY27-29E. The market and the one broker with a record of calls value Olectra on P/E: the stock's 64.3x forward-P/E median since Apr-2021, cut by the 6.9% auto-OEM de-rating, gives **60x Sep-28E EPS of ₹32.6 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): BUY under our rule.** Every window we tested gives a BUY (12-month window 43x ≈ ₹1,400), because the stock now trades at 34.7x. The cross-checks split: EV/EBITDA ₹1,884, DCF only ₹273. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Demand is real and Olectra has a seat at the table
arguments.p: Domestic e-bus sales were ~5,400 in FY26 (+30%), ~46,000 buses are awarded for the next 2-3 years and over 10,000 more tenders are expected in 12 months. Olectra sold 1,280 vehicles (~24% share), has an order book of over 8,000 buses (MSRTC ~4,000, BEST ~2,000, TGSRTC 1,085, BMTC 700) and a new plant able to build 5,000 a year.

Evey Trans, a subsidiary of Olectra's own parent, bids for the contracts and buys the buses. Prices are set by "comparable market benchmarking" and were "jointly worked out" with Evey before bidding. Olectra's cash depends on Evey's SPVs drawing project loans and on states paying them; ₹718 cr of its ₹993 cr of receivables were owed by related parties at Mar-26.

arguments.h: Execution, not demand, is the swing factor
arguments.p: Olectra guided ~2,000 vehicles for FY26 and delivered 1,280; MSRTC threatened to cancel its 5,150-bus order in May-2025 and had ~1,200 by Apr-2026. FY27 guidance slipped from 2,500 to 2,000-2,500 between June and August. We assume 1,850 and a Mobility EBIT margin of 9%, below FY25-26.

arguments.h: Cheap against its own past, expensive against its cash
arguments.p: At ₹1,134 Olectra trades at 34.7x our Sep-28E EPS and 52.2x trailing, against a 64.3x forward-P/E median since Apr-2021 and −44% from its Feb-2024 peak. The house rule gives 60x and a BUY; a DCF that holds working capital at ~30% of revenue says ₹273. The target assumes the market keeps paying a growth multiple for a bus maker whose cash flow is negative.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): deliveries against the ~500 management expects for the quarter, the half-year balance sheet and receivables.
MSRTC deliveries against the extended Dec-2026 deadline, and signing of the 700-bus BMTC (Bengaluru) contract that was pending in June.
New bus platform (Q3FY27) and the e-truck launch (Q4FY27, 28-55 tonnes; MEIL as the first customer).
Award of the 10,000+ e-bus tenders the company expects in the 12 months from Jun-2026 (PM E-DRIVE, PM e-Bus Sewa).
Insulator margins: back towards FY26's 34.5% or down to Q1FY27's 22%.

sections.title: Two businesses: electric buses built with BYD technology, and composite insulators

blocks.p: Olectra reports two segments. The **Mobility Division** (86% of FY26 revenue) builds 7, 9 and 12-metre electric buses, intercity coaches and electric tippers, using batteries, chassis and parts from BYD of China under a technology collaboration, and earns service revenue for maintaining them (₹183 cr in FY26). The **Energy Division** (14%) makes composite polymer insulators (66 kV to 800 kV transmission, railway, post and distribution insulators) for Power Grid, transmission contractors and export utilities. The company is 50.02% owned by MEIL Holdings, the holding company of the Megha Engineering & Infrastructures (MEIL) group. Its biggest customer is another MEIL company: Evey Trans, which bids for state bus contracts, sets up one project company (SPV) per contract, buys the buses from Olectra and runs them for 10-12 years.

blocks.p: Indian bus sales 35,000-50,000 a year historically, ~67,000 in FY26 (KPMG, Mar-2026, in AR FY26 MD&A; buses above 7 m). E-buses: 0.6k (FY20), 1.2k (FY22), 3.7k (FY24), 3.5k (FY25), 4.9k (FY26), over 90% bought by state transport undertakings on gross-cost contracts. The company puts FY26 domestic e-bus sales at 5,423 (+~30%) and penetration at 4.7% (9-12 m buses ~9%). ~46,000 e-buses awarded for deployment over 2-3 years (KPMG in AR FY26); over 10,000 more tenders expected in the next 12 months (company, Jun-2026). Schemes: PM e-Bus Sewa (10,000 buses in 169 cities), PM E-DRIVE (CESL tenders, e.g. 1,085 TGSRTC, 700 BMTC), FAME-II earlier. Penetration could reach 35-40% by FY35 (industry estimate quoted in AR FY26).

blocks.p: **How the market works.** Tata Motors (now TML CV), Ashok Leyland's Switch Mobility, PMI Foton, JBM (Solaris platform), EKA, Pinnacle and others (ICRA, Oct-2025). Tenders are priced per kilometre, so the operator (often the maker's group company) carries the contract; makers compete on price per km, financing and delivery. **Insulators.** Indian insulator market ~US$0.5 bn (FY25, AR FY26); demand from 500 GW renewables integration, inter-state transmission and railway electrification. Olectra's Energy Division sells composite polymer insulators to PGCIL, EPC contractors (Kalpataru, L&T) and exports (~37% of FY26 division revenue: Nepal, Niger, Mozambique, Malawi, Tunisia).

blocks.callout: **So what:** demand is set by state budgets and central schemes, and the order goes to the operator that bids the lowest cost per km. A bus maker that belongs to a group with an operator (Olectra with Evey, JBM with JBM Ecolife) wins volume, but its selling price is set inside a group deal, and its cash depends on the operator's funding.

bullets: **Pricing.** AGM 26-Sep-2026 sought approval for sales to Evey Trans (NSK) ₹1,854 cr (80% of FY26 turnover) and Evey Trans (KAR) ₹1,080 cr (47%) over 24 months, plus continuing arrangements with Evey Trans (MSR) and (MAH). Prices set by 'comparable market benchmarking'; Olectra and Evey 'jointly worked out the commercials before bidding'.

**Credit support runs both ways.** Olectra gave REC an irrevocable undertaking for a letter-of-comfort facility used to open LCs for bus components: ₹201.5 cr carved out of the term loan sanctioned to Evey Trans (MSR) and ₹70.5 cr under Evey Trans (MUM); Olectra must repay with interest if buses are not supplied and hypothecated within six months. Shown as a contingent liability of ₹272 cr at Mar-25, nil at Mar-26 (AR FY26 note 32). MEIL in turn guarantees Olectra's plant loan and was asked to lend ₹150 cr for the TGSRTC project.

**Why it worked so far.** ICRA (Oct-2025) notes that working capital improved in FY25 because Evey's SPVs drew project debt faster, and that Olectra usually gets ~60% of the price on or before delivery and the rest in 120-180 days. Olectra's payment therefore depends on Evey raising debt and on states paying Evey.
**What we cannot see.** Evey's accounts, its debt, the per-km fees it earns and the margin Olectra earns on each Evey bus versus a bus sold to a third party are not disclosed.

blocks.callout: **So what:** the arrangement is common in Indian e-buses (JBM does the same with JBM Ecolife) and it fills the factory. But it means the listed company's revenue, margin and receivables are set in deals between companies controlled by the same promoter. We treat the related-party share as an accounting and governance flag (AMBER), not as evidence of wrongdoing: the auditor gave a clean opinion and the large contracts are put to shareholders for approval.

sections.title: Insulators: revenue +81% and EBIT +144% in FY26 on transmission spending; Q1FY27 margin back to 22%

blocks.p: The Energy Division makes composite polymer insulators. Revenue was flat at ₹108-143 cr a year from FY20 to FY24, then rose to ₹180 cr (FY25) and ₹325 cr (FY26) as India's transmission build-out and exports (~37% of FY26 division revenue) took off. Segment EBIT rose from ₹33 cr (FY24) to ₹112 cr (FY26), a 34.5% margin and 37% of group segment EBIT. Q4FY26 was exceptional (₹106 cr at a 37.9% margin); Q1FY27 revenue was ₹81 cr (+47% year on year, −23% on Q4) at 22.1%. Insulator orders are fixed-price, so margins swing with resin and metal costs (ICRA). Management aims to grow the division five-fold in three years with new products (hollow-core insulators for substations) and capacity.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** A narrow, execution-dependent position, not a moat. Olectra has a real installed base (3,800+ vehicles), BYD technology and a plant that can make 5,000 vehicles a year, and its group company Evey wins large gross-cost contracts. But the technology is licensed, tenders are won on price per km by the operator, and the bus maker's margin is set inside a group deal. The insulator business has better economics (25-35% EBIT) but is small.

sections.title: Revenue 8x in five years on e-buses; EPS 22x from a near-zero base, but FY26 profit growth came from insulators

blocks.p: Olectra's consolidated revenue rose from ₹281 cr in FY21 to ₹2,312 cr in FY26 (Screener basis): 52% a year. Almost all of it came from electric vehicles, whose revenue grew from ₹160 cr to ₹1,987 cr as state bus companies moved to e-buses on gross-cost contracts, with Olectra's sister company Evey Trans as the operator. The insulator business, the company's original one, earned ₹108-143 cr a year until FY24 and then jumped to ₹180 cr (FY25) and ₹325 cr (FY26) on transmission spending and exports. The EBITDA margin (Screener basis, before other income) rose from 7% in FY21 to 13-15% from FY22. Net profit attributable to shareholders went from ₹8 cr to ₹177 cr; EPS from ₹0.98 to ₹21.62. In FY26 revenue grew 28% and EPS 28%, but the Mobility Division's segment EBIT rose only 1% (₹193 cr to ₹195 cr): the insulator division's EBIT rose 144% (₹46 cr to ₹112 cr) and supplied almost all of the profit growth.

ROCE (Screener) rose from 2% (FY21) to 21% (FY25-26) as the plant base stayed small; it will fall as the ₹500 cr-plus plant and the new platforms are depreciated.

bullets: **Cash conversion is weak.** Cash from operations was ₹143 cr (FY24), ₹141 cr (FY25) and ₹104 cr (FY26) against net profit of ₹77 / 139 / 177 cr; free cash flow was negative in FY25 and FY26 (Screener).

**Other income is small and real.** FY26 other income ₹14.3 cr: interest ₹11.2 cr (deposits, incl. margin money), FX gain ₹2.1 cr, miscellaneous ₹1.0 cr (AR FY26 note 23). Screener adds the share of associates' profit (₹8.1 cr) to reach ₹22.4 cr. It was 9% of FY26 PBT; we model ₹20 / 22 / 24 cr (four quarters to Jun-26: ₹20 cr).

**Interest was capitalised.** FY26 finance costs ₹61.3 cr: working-capital interest ₹36.5 cr, bank charges and commissions ₹14.8 cr, other borrowing costs ₹8.8 cr, term loans ₹1.2 cr; ₹13.7 cr of interest capitalised into the new plant (AR FY26 notes 17 and 29). That flattered FY26 PBT by ~₹14 cr (~6%).

**Segment results include other income.** Segment EBIT less (EBITDA − depreciation) was ₹19 cr (FY24), ₹14 cr (FY25), ₹22 cr (FY26), matching other income incl. associates; our build deducts it (₹20 / 22 / 24 cr).

**Warranties are growing.** Sarath & Associates, Chartered Accountants; unmodified opinion on FY26. Key audit matters: recoverability of trade receivables (gross ₹987 cr in the holding company) and warranty provisions (₹14.9 cr charged in FY26; ₹43.3 cr outstanding).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** No qualification, small exceptional items and other income that is mostly deposit interest. But the profit is earned largely on sales to companies controlled by Olectra's own promoter, at prices set with them, and paid for when their lenders and the states pay. That is a quality issue even if every transaction is at arm's length.

sections.title: The street: one standing target (₹1,750, Jul-2026) and an expired Geojit call

blocks.p: Coverage is very thin. Trendlyne lists six notes on Olectra, all from Geojit BNP Paribas; the latest is dated 21-Aug-2025 (Accumulate, target ₹1,732, a 12-month target that had expired by our as-of date; the excerpt gives the FY26 delivery plan of ~2,000 buses and the 10,000-bus order book but no multiple). Nomura and Axis Capital hosted the company's calls in 2024-25; we found no published targets from them. sections.title: Our honest summary: a real e-bus franchise run through the parent's operator, at 35x Sep-28E EPS; BUY on the house multiple

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's first and one of its two or three largest e-bus makers (~24% of FY26 units), an order book of over 8,000 buses, a new plant able to make 5,000 vehicles a year, an insulator business with 25-35% margins, and a parent (MEIL) that funds the operator, guarantees the plant loan and will be the first e-truck customer. If deliveries double, EPS can grow ~20% a year to FY29E.

**What you are paying:** 54.5x our FY27E and 38.7x FY28E EPS for a business with a ~12% EBITDA margin, negative free cash flow and three-quarters of its sales going to its own group. That is cheap against the stock's 64.3x forward-P/E median since Apr-2021, which is why our rule gives BUY with a target of {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). It is not cheap against cash: the DCF says ₹273.

assumptions._interestLabel: Finance costs (working-capital loans, plant term loan, bank charges)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs61 cr after Rs13.7 cr was capitalised into the new plant; Q1FY27 Rs23.6 cr (+97%) once capitalisation stopped and working-capital loans rose. FY27E Rs95 cr (Q1 x4); Rs110-115 cr in FY28-29E as working capital and the platform/truck capex lift net debt in our model.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective tax plus the minority share: FY26 27.9% (tax 27.1% + minorities 0.8%), FY25 26.1%, Q1FY27 25.3%. 26.5%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs0.60 a share on EPS Rs21.62 (2.8%); FY25 Rs0.40.

build._note: Two-segment build (Rs crore). FY26 base = AR FY26 note 34. Mobility revenue = vehicles x revenue per vehicle (includes services, spares and bus-operation revenue). Segment EBIT is profit before interest and tax as reported; it includes other income and the associates' share, so bridge = otherIncome (FY24 Rs19 cr, FY25 Rs14 cr, FY26 Rs22 cr, Q1FY27 Rs5 cr: see OLECTRA.ctx.js).
build._why: Vehicles: FY26 1,280 (+32%); Q1FY27 358 (+122%). Guidance 2,000-2,500 for FY27; Olectra delivered 64% of its FY26 target (~2,000 guided, 1,280 delivered; MSRTC deliveries ~1,200 of 5,150 by Apr-2026), so 1,850 / 2,400 / 2,800 (FY29E = 56% of the 5,000 plant). Revenue per vehicle Rs1.40 / 1.43 / 1.46 cr (FY26 Rs1.55 cr, Q1FY27 Rs1.38 cr; more 9-metre buses in the TGSRTC/BMTC orders, trucks from Q4FY27). Mobility EBIT 9.0% / 9.5% / 9.5%: Q1FY27 8.2%, FY26 9.8%, FY25 11.9%; tender pricing and a new plant's fixed costs offset softer raw materials. Insulators: FY26 +81% (Rs325 cr) with a 34.5% EBIT margin, Q1FY27 +47% but 22.1%; management targets 5x revenue in three years (new products, capacity, exports): +20% / +18% / +15% at 24%.

dcf._betaWhy: Tender-driven volumes, one group customer (Evey) for most sales, technology dependence on BYD and a small-cap retail-held stock. Net debt is small (~2-5% of enterprise value), so WACC is close to the cost of equity; beta 1.15 gives 13.4%.
dcf._tgWhy: House range 5-6%: 6%, as bus electrification has decades to run (penetration ~5-7% in FY26).
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~18% to 9% over ten years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin 11% in steady state: management's own long-run band is 10-12%.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 3% of revenue (FY24-26: 7-15% while the plant was built); depreciation 2.2%. Working capital stays at ~30% of revenue (the engine holds the FY26 ratio).

bull.narrative: Deliveries hit guidance (2,300+ in FY27E, 3,500 by FY29E) as MSRTC, BEST and TGSRTC buses flow from the new plant, e-trucks find MEIL and outside buyers, and insulators keep FY26-like margins: growth ~8pp a year higher and EBITDA margin +1pp.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Execution slips again (depots, BYD parts, Evey's funding), MSRTC or another STU cancels part of an order, Evey pays more slowly so Olectra borrows more, and tender prices squeeze margins: growth ~10pp a year lower and EBITDA margin -1.5pp.
